questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Principal Normal at a Given Point
questions.problem:
The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+{t}^{2}}}⟨1,t⟩.
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+{t}^{2}}}⟨1,t⟩) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+{t}^{2}}})⟨1,t⟩+\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+{t}^{2}}}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =-\frac{t}{(1+{t}^{2})^{3/2}}⟨1,t⟩+\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+{t}^{2}}}⟨0,1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{(1+{t}^{2})^{3/2}}[-t⟨1,t⟩+(1+{t}^{2})⟨0,1⟩] \\  & =\frac{1}{(1+{t}^{2})^{3/2}}⟨-t,1⟩ \\  \\ {T}^{′}(1) & =\frac{1}{(1+{1}^{2})^{3/2}}⟨-1,1⟩ \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}⟨-1,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(1)‖ & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}‖⟨-1,1⟩‖ \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the principal normal vector to the curve at the point where $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(1) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(1)}{‖{T}^{′}(1)‖}=\frac{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}⟨-1,1⟩}{\frac{1}{2}}=⟨-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=1,$  we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1)\cdot N(1) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,1⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The equations of a curve $r(t)$ and its corresponding unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at an arbitrary point are given below. Find the principal normal vector to that curve at the point $P(0,3,4).$

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k,\,t\in [0,2\pi ) \\ T(t) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,k,\,t\in [0,2\pi )\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(0,3,4)$ on the given curve. We know that:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨0,3,4⟩ \\ 5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k & =0\text{ }i+3\text{ }j+4\text{ }k\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the components of $i$, $j$, and $k$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}5\operatorname{cos}⁡t=0 \\ 3\operatorname{sin}⁡t=3 \\ 4\operatorname{sin}⁡t=4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equality, $t=\frac{\pi }{2}.$ This value also satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, $P(0,3,4)$ is at the tip of the vector $r(\frac{\pi }{2}).$ 

Now, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\frac{\pi }{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,k \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k \\ {T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}\,i-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}\,j-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}\,k \\  & =-\frac{3}{5}\,j-\frac{4}{5}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖ & =\sqrt{(0)^{2}+{(-\frac{3}{5})}^{2}+{(-\frac{4}{5})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{9}{25}+\frac{16}{25}} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve $r(t)$ at the point $P(0,3,4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})}{‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖}=\frac{-\frac{3}{5}\,j-\frac{4}{5}\,k}{1}=-\frac{3}{5}\,j-\frac{4}{5}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where at $t=\frac{\pi }{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\frac{\pi }{2})\cdot N(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =(-i)\cdot (-\frac{3}{5}\,j-\frac{4}{5}\,k) \\  & =\frac{3}{5}(i\cdot j)+\frac{4}{5}(i\cdot k) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+16}}\cdot ⟨t,4⟩.
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=0.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+16}}\cdot ⟨t,4⟩) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+16}})\cdot ⟨t,4⟩+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+16}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(⟨t,4⟩) \\  & =-\frac{t}{({t}^{2}+16)\sqrt{{t}^{2}+16}}\cdot ⟨t,4⟩+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+16}}\cdot ⟨1,0⟩ \\  \\ {T}^{′}(0) & =-\frac{0}{({0}^{2}+16)\sqrt{{0}^{2}+16}}\cdot ⟨0,4⟩+\frac{1}{\sqrt{{0}^{2}+16}}\cdot ⟨1,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}⟨1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

  

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(0)‖ & =\frac{1}{4}‖⟨1,0⟩‖ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(0)$ and obtain the principal normal vector to the curve at the point where $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(0) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(0)}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{4}⟨1,0⟩}{(\frac{1}{4})} \\  & =⟨1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0)\cdot N(0) & =\frac{1}{4}⟨0,4⟩\cdot ⟨1,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(0+0) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+1}}⟨1,\,2t⟩.
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+1}}⟨1,\,2t⟩) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+1}})⟨1,\,2t⟩+\frac{1}{\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+1}}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)⟩ \\  & =-\frac{4t}{(4{t}^{2}+1)^{3/2}}⟨1,\,2t⟩+\frac{1}{(4{t}^{2}+1)^{1/2}}⟨0,\,2⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{(4{t}^{2}+1)^{3/2}}[-4t⟨1,\,2t⟩+(4{t}^{2}+1)⟨0,\,2⟩] \\  & =\frac{1}{(4{t}^{2}+1)^{3/2}}⟨-4t,\,2\,⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(1) & =\frac{1}{(4(1)^{2}+1)^{3/2}}⟨-4(1),\,2⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{{5}^{3}}}⟨-4,2⟩ \\  & =\frac{2}{5\sqrt{5}}⟨-2,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(1)‖ & =\frac{2}{5\sqrt{5}}‖⟨-2,1⟩‖ \\  & =\frac{2}{5\sqrt{5}}\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+(1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{5\sqrt{5}}\sqrt{5} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the principal normal vector to the curve at the point where $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(1) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(1)}{‖{T}^{′}(1)‖}=\frac{\frac{2}{5\sqrt{5}}⟨-2,1⟩}{(\frac{2}{5})}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨-2,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $N$ and $T$ at the point where $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}N(1)\cdot T(1) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨-2,1⟩\cdot (\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨1,\,2⟩) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(⟨-2,1⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,2⟩) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}((-2)(1)+(1)(2)) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩.
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{6}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\frac{\pi }{6}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩) \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6}) & =⟨-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}),\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,-\sqrt{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6})‖ & =‖⟨-1,-\sqrt{3}⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(\sqrt{3})^{2}} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6})$ and obtain the principal normal vector to the curve at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{6}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(\frac{\pi }{6}) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6})}{‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6})‖} \\  & =\frac{⟨-1,-\sqrt{3}⟩}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨-1,-\sqrt{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $N$ and $T$ at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{6},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\frac{\pi }{6})\cdot N(\frac{\pi }{6}) & =⟨-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\frac{1}{2}⟩\cdot \frac{1}{2}⟨-1,-\sqrt{3}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}((-\sqrt{3})(-1)+(1)(-\sqrt{3})) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
T(t)=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.
$$

The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given above. Find the principal normal vector to that curve at an arbitrary point on the curve.

$N(t)=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$
$⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t,$
{{field-1}}
$⟩$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =|-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}|‖⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩‖ \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\sqrt{{(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\sqrt{2({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩}{1} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given the curve $r(t)=⟨5\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,5\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,12t⟩$, find the principal normal vector $N(t)$ at an arbitrary point on the curve.

$N(t)=⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,$
{{field-1}}$,0\,⟩$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the unit tangent vector $T(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(12t)⟩ \\  & =⟨5\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-5\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,12⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(5\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(-5\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(12)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{25({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)+144} \\  & =\sqrt{25(1)+144} \\  & =\sqrt{169} \\  & =13\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{13}⟨5\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-5\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,12⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{5}{13}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\frac{5}{13}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\frac{12}{13}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal normal $N(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{5}{13}\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{5}{13}\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{12}{13})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{5}{13}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\frac{5}{13}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,0⟩ \\  & =-\frac{5}{13}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,0⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-\frac{5}{13}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-\frac{5}{13}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{25}{169}({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\frac{5}{13}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{-\frac{5}{13}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,0⟩}{(\frac{5}{13})}=⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given the curve $r(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+2\sqrt{2}\,t\,k$, find the principal normal vector $N(t)$ at an arbitrary point on the curve.

$N(t)=$
{{field-1}}
$i\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t$

$j$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the unit tangent vector $T(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\sqrt{2}\,t)\,k \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+2\sqrt{2}\,k \\  \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(2\sqrt{2})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t+8} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+2\sqrt{2}\,k}{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{2}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal normal $N(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{1}{3}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i-\frac{1}{3}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{2})\,k \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+0\,k \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j \\  \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{9}({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j}{(\frac{1}{3})} \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Given  the curve $r(t)=⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,4t⟩$, find the principal normal vector $N(t)$ at an arbitrary point on the curve.

$N(t)=⟨\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,$
{{field-1}}$,0\,⟩$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the unit tangent vector $T(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,4⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(4)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)+16} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,4⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\frac{4}{5}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal normal $N(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{4}{5})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩ \\  & =-\frac{3}{5}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{9}{25}({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}\cdot q(t).
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=1$, if 

$$
\begin{aligned}q(1)=-i+j+\sqrt{2}\,k,\,{q}^{′}(1)=2\,j+\sqrt{2}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}\cdot q(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1})\cdot q(t)+\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(q(t)) \\  & =-\frac{2t}{({t}^{2}+1)^{2}}\cdot q(t)+\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}\cdot {q}^{′}(t) \\  \\ {T}^{′}(1) & =-\frac{2(1)}{({1}^{2}+1)^{2}}\cdot q(1)+\frac{1}{{1}^{2}+1}\cdot {q}^{′}(1) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}(-i+j+\sqrt{2}\,k)+\frac{1}{2}(2\,j+\sqrt{2}\,k) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(i+j)\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(1)‖ & =|\frac{1}{2}|\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(1)^{2}+(0)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve at the point where $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(1) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(1)}{‖{T}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{2}(i+j)}{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(i+j)\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $N$ and $T$ at the point where $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1)\cdot N(1) & =\frac{1}{2}q(1)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(i+j) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-i+j+\sqrt{2}\,k)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(i+j) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}(-1+1+0) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(0)‖ & =\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(0) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(0)}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{4}⟨1,0,-1⟩}{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4})} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,0,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0)\cdot N(0) & =\frac{1}{2}q(0)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,0,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨1,\sqrt{2},1⟩\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨1,0,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}(1(1)+\sqrt{2}(0)+1(-1)) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}(1+0-1) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}

The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+4t}}\cdot q(t).

$$
\begin{aligned}q(2)=⟨1,2\sqrt{2}⟩,\,{q}^{′}(2)=⟨0,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+4t}}\cdot q(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+4t}})\cdot q(t)+\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+4t}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(q(t)) \\  & =-\frac{2}{(1+4t)^{3/2}}\cdot q(t)+\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+4t}}\cdot {q}^{′}(t) \\  \\ {T}^{′}(2) & =-\frac{2}{(1+4(2))^{3/2}}\cdot q(2)+\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+4(2)}}\cdot {q}^{′}(2) \\  & =-\frac{2}{27}⟨1,2\sqrt{2}⟩+\frac{1}{3}⟨0,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{27}(-2⟨1,2\sqrt{2}⟩+9⟨0,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟩) \\  & =\frac{1}{27}⟨-2,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{54}⟨-4,\sqrt{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(2)‖ & =\frac{1}{54}\sqrt{(-4)^{2}+(\sqrt{2})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{54}\cdot \sqrt{18} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{18}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(2)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve at the point where $t=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(2) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(2)}{‖{T}^{′}(2)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{54}⟨-4,\sqrt{2}⟩}{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{18})} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}}⟨-4,\sqrt{2}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨-2\sqrt{2},1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(2)\cdot N(2) & =\frac{1}{3}q(2)\cdot \frac{1}{3}⟨-2\sqrt{2},1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨1,2\sqrt{2}⟩\cdot \frac{1}{3}⟨-2\sqrt{2},1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{9}(1\cdot (-2\sqrt{2})+2\sqrt{2}\cdot 1) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}(-2\sqrt{2}+2\sqrt{2}) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(0) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(0)}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{-j+k}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(-j+k)\end{aligned}

canonical_examples.problem:
The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
\mathbf T(t) =\sin{t} \,\mathbf i -\cos{t}\,\mathbf j.
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=\dfrac{\pi}{4}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Remember that in general, the principal normal vector is given by

$$
\mathbf N(t)= \dfrac{\mathbf T'(t)}{\|\mathbf T'(t)\|}.
$$

First, we calculate $\mathbf T'(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\dfrac{\pi}{4}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j \\ {T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\,j \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,i+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,j \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(i+j)\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of $\mathbf T'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖ & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}‖i+j‖ \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\sqrt{{(1)}^{2}+{(1)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\sqrt{2} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize $\mathbf T'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$ and obtain the principal normal vector to the curve at the point where $t=\dfrac{\pi}{4}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})}{‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖}=\frac{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(i+j)}{1}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,i+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

To check our result, we can verify that $\mathbf T$ and $\mathbf N$ are perpendicular by computing their dot product:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\frac{\pi }{4})\cdot N(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,i-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,j)\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,i+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,j) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =0\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Given  the curve $\mathbf r(t)=\left\langle \sqrt 3 t , \:  \cos t, \: \sin{t}\right\rangle,$ find the principal normal vector $\mathbf N(t)$ at an arbitrary point on the curve.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Remember that in general, the principal normal vector is given by

$$
\mathbf N(t)= \dfrac{\mathbf T'(t)}{\|\mathbf T'(t)\|}.
$$

First, we find the unit tangent vector $\mathbf T(t).$ To do this, we calculate $\mathbf r'(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{3}t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{3},\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(\sqrt{3})^{2}+(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{3+{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\sqrt{3},\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\,-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{2},\,\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal normal $\mathbf{N}(t).$ To do this, we calculate $\mathbf T'(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨0,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize $\mathbf T'(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{\frac{1}{2}⟨0,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩}{(\frac{1}{2})}=⟨0,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To check our result, we can verify that $\mathbf T$ and $\mathbf N$ are perpendicular by computing their dot product:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t)\cdot N(t) & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\,-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{2},\,\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{2}⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot 0+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{2}-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{2} \\  & =0\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
